_what: FEATURE SPEC v3: EYES with real depth and colour (felid pack, case cat1, cat v3). The V3_BRIEF eye standard as a buildable spec: optics (cornea, tear film, anterior chamber, iris, pupil, lens, sclera, limbus), the Cycles material plan, probes with planted failures, and the fixes for the Phase 2 eye defects (goggle step, jagged lid rim, eyelid_wrap input contract). Spec only: no geometry, Blender not touched. Builds ON spec_eyes.json (globe, lid margin, lids, third eyelid) and feat_eyes.py; every value there that is not overridden here stands.
status: spec (self-checked; not independently reviewed). Written by the eye-spec-v3 agent, unix 1792341346 to 1792342387.
labels: checked = measured here with a script kept in cases/cat1/lab/eyes_v3/ | cited = a published value (sources) | derived = arithmetic on cited/checked values | estimate = no source; flagged, low confidence | unchecked = stated, not measured

cornea_may_bulge.person: yes, eyeballs cornea may bulge past Tripo's flat painted eye - if that's what it's meant to do in a realistic eyeball
cornea_may_bulge.check: D1: cornea shape = cited anatomy (feat_eyes.probe_globe_shape: r 8.82 +-0.5 by circle fit, apex within 0.5 mm of spec_eyes, axial length 19.75 +-0.3). The bulge in front of Tripo's cap is reported as information (Phase 2: apex 1.48 L / 1.38 R mm outside Tripo, feat_eyes probes.json). C3 applies to the SKIN only.

real_depth_and_colour.person: we want the eyes to have real depth and color
real_depth_and_colour.check: D2 = probes R1 (parallax depth), R2 (iris colour dE00 vs photo), R3 (pupil from the photo), R5 (corneal caustic). All four must PASS.

unseen_side_rule: The person's direction (NOTES_v3 09:45): the unseen side comes from a fitted model of the CLASS, never a flat slab or a mirror. For the eye the photo sees only the front of the cornea, the iris through it and the pupil. Everything behind (posterior cornea, aqueous depth, iris profile and back, lens, vitreous, fundus, posterior sclera) is taken from the cat's cited ocular biometry (a schematic cat eye), labelled per value below. Nothing is painted onto the cornea to fake depth.
frame: head-frame mm as spec_eyes.json (x = cat's LEFT, y = BACK, z = UP); per eye the eye frame (n axis, u lateral, v up) and sclera centre Cs from spec_eyes.json eyes.<side>.globe. 'depth' below = distance BEHIND the corneal apex along -n. Apex = Cs + 10.30 n (sag 5.70 at the 8.25 mm limbus radius, limbus plane 4.61 in front of Cs; spec_eyes globe_derivation). Blender scene units are metres: multiply mm by 0.001.

photo_reading._how: checked: cases/cat1/lab/eyes_v3/eye_photo2.py on cases/cat1/ref.jpg (sRGB -> CIELAB D65, skimage). Regions inside the inner dark-rim ellipses of spec_eyes.json photo.inner_rim_ellipse_px (rms 0.4-0.5 px). Figures: eyes_crop_x8.png, eye_masks.png. Image R = the cat's right eye (image left).

eye_colour.answer: BLUE. Both irises are a light-to-medium slate / steel blue, greyer and darker at the periphery (limbal ring) and lighter in the lower half. This confirms the lilac-point expectation (pointed cats are blue-eyed).

radial_profile_rho_L_a_b._rho: normalised to the inner-rim ellipse (1 = the dark rim), body pixels only

eye_colour.reading: Hue and chroma agree between the eyes (hue -100 to -105 deg, C* 14.5-15.3); lightness differs by 14.6 L*. One cat has one iris colour, so the L* difference is LIGHTING (the key light comes from the camera's upper right; the R eye sits further from it and under more lid shadow). The photo colour is therefore appearance, not albedo: the albedo is FITTED by rendering under the photo light (probe R2), not copied.
eye_colour.label: checked (photo measures); albedo = to be fitted (estimate until R2 runs)

pupil.shape: a VERTICAL ellipse with POINTED poles (lens / vesica outline), mid-dilated. Not a slit and not round. Widths at a quarter and three quarters of its height are 4-8 and 12-13 px against a 14-15 px maximum: the top pole is pointed.

apparent_px.threshold: L* < 22 (half-way between the pupil's L* 5-7 and the darker iris), connected to the centre, highlight excluded; at L* < 15 / < 30 the height is 24-25 / 26-27 px and the width 14 / 16-20 px

pupil.apparent_mm: height 24-27 px x 0.367-0.39 mm/px = 8.8-10.5 mm; width 14-15 px = 5.1-5.9 mm (photo-scale spread from spec_eyes and check_eyes)

true_mm.derivation: apparent / corneal magnification 1.154 (paraxial, two-surface cornea, pupil plane 4.66 mm behind the apex; see optics.paraxial). The view is ~14-16 deg off each eye's axis (spec_eyes), which foreshortens by cos 15 = 0.97: within the range. The builder REPLACES these by fitting the pupil outline through the built cornea to the photo outline (probe R3: fit on L, hold out R)
true_mm.label: derived (estimate until R3 fits it)

pupil.position: pupil centres sit 4-5.5 px (1.5-2.1 mm) ABOVE the inner-rim ellipse centres and 0.5 (R) / 2.0 (L) px medial (checked). The rim ellipse is the LID opening, not the limbus, so this offset is not a decentred pupil. Starting value: spec_eyes photo.pupil_on_globe_UV_mm (L [-1.69, 1.3], R [-1.15, 1.31]), which was NOT refraction-corrected (estimate). The builder back-projects the photo pupil centre through the built cornea (ray trace).

corneal_highlight.reading: one crisp, compact highlight per eye, upper RIGHT in the image on both eyes (one key light at the camera's upper right; medial-up on R, lateral-up on L). Crisp and saturated: a wet, smooth, strongly curved cornea (tear film).
corneal_highlight.label: checked

corneal_caustic.what: a bright crescent in the LOWER-LEFT iris periphery, opposite the highlight, on both eyes: L* 74-75, rho >= 0.6. It is the key light focused through the curved cornea onto the iris (a refractive caustic), a standard depth cue of real eyes.
corneal_caustic.consequence: the render must carry refractive caustics through the cornea (materials_cycles.lighting). A shadow-ray-transparent cornea cannot produce it.
corneal_caustic.label: checked

photo_reading.sclera: no white sclera is visible: the iris fills the opening to the dark lid rim (normal for a cat looking ahead). Sclera colour below is therefore an estimate.
photo_reading.dark_rim: the 0.85-1.3 mm dark band round the opening is the pigmented LID MARGIN (spec_eyes photo_findings), owned by the skin and pigment, not by the eye.

globe.value: unchanged from spec_eyes.json: sclera sphere RS 9.45, cornea r 8.82, limbus diameter 16.5, axial length 19.75, apex 10.30 in front of Cs, limbal blend 0.8
globe.label: cited/derived (spec_eyes)

central_thickness_mm.source: cited: Gilger et al. 1993, ultrasonic pachymetry, 35 cats / 70 eyes (PMID 8430933). Cross-check: 0.623 +- 0.048, 18 cats, 2023 (higher; device-dependent)
central_thickness_mm.label: cited

thickness_profile.source: cited: central and peripheral thickness did not differ significantly (Gilger 1993)
thickness_profile.label: derived

refractive_index.source: the brief's value: human schematic eye (Le Grand / Gullstrand). The cat-specific schematic eye is Bishop, Kozak & Vakkur 1962, J Physiol 163:466 (PMC1359720), not read
refractive_index.label: cited (human), adopted for the cat

tear_film.thickness: micrometres (human ~3-10 um; no feline value found): NOT geometry, rendered as a clear coat on the anterior cornea

meniscus.what: the strip of tear fluid along the lower lid margin (a wet glint line)
meniscus.label: estimate (human tear-meniscus height ~0.2-0.3 mm; no feline value)
meniscus.build: optional thin glass strip along the lower margin from canthus to canthus; off if it fails the lid probes

tear_film.label: estimate (index cited for human tears)

anterior_chamber_length_mm.source: cited: Konrade et al. 2012, A-mode ultrasound, 98 cats (PMID 22280390): axial length 19.75 +- 1.59, anterior chamber length 4.66 +- 0.86, vitreous chamber 7.92 +- 0.86
anterior_chamber_length_mm.convention: taken as anterior corneal surface -> anterior lens capsule (the usual A-mode length). If it is posterior cornea -> lens, add 0.58 (pupil plane 5.24 behind the apex). The apparent-depth probe R1 tolerance covers neither alternative, so the builder states which it used; default 4.66
anterior_chamber_length_mm.label: cited (convention estimate)

anterior_chamber.iridocorneal_angle: the iris root inserts at the angle recess just inside and behind the limbus (estimate: root radius 8.0 mm from the axis, 5.6 mm behind the apex; the limbus plane is 5.70 behind the apex)

root_diameter_mm.label: estimate (0.25 mm inside the cited 16.5 limbus)

profile.value: a shallow forward-convex cone resting on the lens: pupil margin ON the anterior lens surface at the pupil plane (4.66 behind the apex), root at r 8.0 / depth 5.6
profile.label: derived (pupil plane cited; root estimate)

thickness_mm.taper: 0.2 at the pupil margin, 0.4 at mid-iris, 0.3 at the root
thickness_mm.label: estimate (no feline value found)

front_relief_mm.what: radial stromal fibres (trabeculae) and crypts as a bump/height field
front_relief_mm.label: estimate (below the photo's 0.37 mm/px; class prior)

radial_fibres.collarette: a faint lighter ring at 30-35 % of the way from pupil margin to root
radial_fibres.label: estimate (class prior; photo cannot resolve; flagged)

iris.colour: from the photo (photo_reading.eye_colour) via the material fit; posterior surface = pigment epithelium, near-black brown (albedo 0.03, estimate)
iris.apparent_vs_true: everything seen of the iris is seen THROUGH the cornea: apparent size = true x 1.154 at the pupil plane (paraxial), shifted 0.64 mm forward. The photo crop must never be projected straight onto the iris; texels are mapped by ray tracing through the built cornea (materials_cycles.iris.texture).

pupil.shape_model: vesica / pointed ellipse. Half-width at height y: x(y) = (w/2) * (1 - |2y/h|^k)^(1/k) * (1 - pinch*|2y/h|^2), k = 2, pinch fitted (photo: the quarter-height widths 4-8 / 12-13 of a 14-15 max => pinch ~0.3, estimate). Parameters (h, w, pinch) are RIG controls: slit (bright) to round (dark); the cat's slit pupil changes area ~135-fold (Banks et al. 2015 Sci Adv; cited)
pupil.label: shape checked on the photo; parameters derived/estimate until fitted

thickness_mm.source: derived: axial length 19.75 - anterior chamber 4.66 - vitreous 7.92 (Konrade 2012). Cross-checks: 6.8 mm (a 2009 30-cat ultrasound study, different scheme); leopard cat 8.1 mm
thickness_mm.label: derived

anterior_radius_mm.label: estimate (chosen with the posterior radius to give the derived thickness at an 11.5 mm equator)

equivalent_index.label: estimate (human equivalent index; the cat's is not found). Appearance-insensitive: through the pupil the fundus reads black (probe R3)

lens.position: anterior pole at the pupil plane (4.66 behind the apex), posterior pole 11.83 behind the apex; vitreous 7.92 behind it to the retina at 19.75 (derived, closes the axial length)

fundus.tapetum: off by default. Cats have a tapetum lucidum (eyeshine), but the photo's pupils read black (L* 4.6-7.3) under off-axis studio light; pointed blue-eyed cats often have a reduced tapetum. A tapetum layer is an option for a coaxial-flash render only
fundus.label: estimate

sclera.perilimbal_band: grey-brown conjunctival pigment band 1.0 mm wide at the limbus, 25 % darker (common in cats)
sclera.label: estimate (no sclera visible in the photo)

limbus.geometry: the 0.8 mm limbal blend of spec_eyes (sulcus between the cornea and sclera spheres)
limbus.optics: the cornea turns opaque across the limbus: transmission fades to the sclera shader over 0.8 mm (radial mask on the distance from the axis, 7.85 -> 8.65 mm)
limbus.look: the photo's darker, greyer iris periphery (rho 0.85: L* -4..-3.6 below the mid-iris, b* 2-3 less blue) is the iris's own limbal ring plus this fade
limbus.label: geometry derived; fade width estimate; ring checked on the photo

paraxial._what: checked arithmetic (scratch script; values below): an object at the pupil plane d behind the apex, imaged out through the posterior cornea (r 8.24, 1.336 -> 1.376) and the anterior cornea (r 8.82, 1.376 -> 1.0)
paraxial.single_surface_check: a single keratometric surface (n 1.336, r 8.82) gives 4.023 / 1.153: the posterior cornea changes < 0.1 %
paraxial.note: the corneal highlight (Purkinje I) of a distant light lies at r/2 = 4.41 mm behind the apex, nearly the same apparent depth as the pupil (4.02): highlight and pupil move almost together under a co-moving light, so the highlight is NOT a parallax reference. R1 uses the camera geometry instead.

geometry_build._rule: per eye, separate objects (never unioned with the skin; the globe rotates). Their OUTER surface (sclera + anterior cornea) must equal feat_eyes.globe_field's globe so the Phase 2 socket, lid and third-eyelid edits and probes stay valid.

objects.name: Eye_<side>_sclera
objects.what: closed globe shell from the limbus back (feat_eyes globe minus the corneal cap), outward normals; its inside face toward the vitreous carries FUNDUS behind the lens

objects.name: Eye_<side>_cornea_front
objects.what: open cap: anterior cornea sphere r 8.82 from the apex to the limbus, merged into the sclera at the limbal blend; normals toward the AIR

objects.name: Eye_<side>_cornea_back
objects.what: open cap: posterior cornea r 8.24 concentric (CCT 0.578), from the axis to the angle, sealed to the iris root so no ray leaks between them; normals toward the AQUEOUS (backward)

objects.name: Eye_<side>_iris
objects.what: annular shell, thickness 0.2-0.4 mm, front surface the cone of optics.iris.profile, inner edge = the pupil outline (optics.pupil) lying on the anterior lens; polar UV (u = angle / 2pi, v = 0 at the pupil margin -> 1 at the root); separate back material

objects.name: Eye_<side>_lens_front / lens_back
objects.what: open caps r 7.0 / 6.0 joined at the 11.5 mm equator (a closed lens is fine too); lens_front normals toward the aqueous (forward), lens_back normals toward the vitreous (backward)

geometry_build.resolution: analytic surfaces meshed at <= 0.10 mm edge length on the cornea and the pupil edge (the highlight and refraction need smooth normals: shade smooth; no marching-cubes faceting on the cornea), <= 0.2 mm elsewhere
geometry_build.parenting: all eye objects share one empty at Cs (the future eye bone): rotating it rotates the whole optical stack

materials_cycles._nested_dielectrics: Cycles has no IOR priority for nested media, so every optical INTERFACE is its own open surface with the ratio of the two indices. Rule: the normal points to the LOWER-index side and IOR = n_high / n_low (>= 1). Cycles then refracts correctly in both directions (entering uses IOR, exiting 1/IOR).

shaders.CORNEA_FRONT: Principled BSDF: Base Color 1,1,1; Transmission Weight 1.0; IOR 1.376; Roughness 0.0; Coat Weight 1.0, Coat IOR 1.337, Coat Roughness 0.01 (the TEAR FILM); across the limbus mix to SCLERA with the 0.8 mm radial mask (optics.limbus). Shade smooth.
shaders.CORNEA_BACK: Refraction BSDF (or Glass BSDF), IOR 1.0299, Roughness 0, white
shaders.IRIS: Principled BSDF, no transmission: Base Color = IRIS_TEX; Roughness 0.45; Subsurface Weight 0.05 (blue stromal scatter, estimate); Normal from Bump(height = fibre field, Distance 0.0001 m = 0.1 mm relief)
shaders.IRIS_TEX: (1) BASE RAMP: the photo radial profile (photo_reading.eye_colour.radial_profile_rho_L_a_b) converted Lab -> linear RGB, as a ColorRamp on v (pupil margin -> root), pupil-side and limbal-ring zones included. (2) PHOTO DETAIL: optional high-pass (> 1 mm wavelength removed) of the de-lit photo crop, mapped by ray tracing each iris texel through the built cornea to the photo (registration by the photo's own rim and pupil ellipses, not by camera_tripo.json, which failed its hold-out), highlight (L* > 75 near the pupil) and caustic crescent masked and inpainted. (3) FIBRES: Wave/Noise texture on (u x 60, v x 2) -> radial streaks, colour x [0.85, 1.15]; Voronoi crypts (scale 12-20 per iris) 10 % darker; collarette ring at v 0.30-0.35 5 % lighter. (4) ALBEDO SCALE: one multiplier on the base ramp (and optionally one on its chroma) FITTED by probe R2 on the L eye; the R eye is the hold-out (chosen now, before any fit; A23).
shaders.SCLERA: Principled BSDF: Base Color sRGB 0.86, 0.82, 0.80 (estimate); Subsurface Weight 1.0, Subsurface Radius (1.0, 0.45, 0.25), Subsurface Scale 0.001 (mm-scale radii in a metre scene); Roughness 0.35; Coat Weight 1.0, Coat Roughness 0.03 (wet conjunctiva); perilimbal band (optics.sclera)

lighting.photo_light: cases/cat1/light.json (key 155, fill 2.13, rim 80, top 6.53, world 0.147, exposure -1.91, Filmic, Very High Contrast) - the same rig the pigment check uses
lighting.caustics: PRIMARY: Cycles MNEE shadow caustics - cornea_front and cornea_back objects 'Cast Shadow Caustics', iris and sclera 'Receive Shadow Caustics', the key light 'Shadow Caustics' on; Light Paths: Refractive and Reflective caustics ON, Filter Glossy 0.0 for probe renders. The builder first verifies MNEE handles the two-interface cornea stack in this Blender build (a test render must show the caustic crescent, probe R5). FALLBACK (previews only): on CORNEA_* and LENS_* mix to a Transparent BSDF when Light Path 'Is Shadow Ray' - the iris is lit but has NO caustic, so R5 FAILS and is reported as a known limitation, never hidden.
lighting.light_paths: Max Bounces 16; Diffuse 4; Glossy 8; Transmission 16; Transparent 16
lighting.sampling: probe renders >= 1024 spp, denoiser OFF (a denoiser can erase the caustic and the fibres); look renders may denoise (OpenImageDenoise with albedo + normal passes)

probes._rules: Each probe is proven on planted failures on both sides (A22) before its PASS counts. Geometry probes read meshes in head-frame mm. Render probes use Cycles with materials_cycles. Photo-side render probes register the rendered eye to the photo eye by the eye's OWN rim and pupil ellipses (a 2-D similarity), because camera_tripo.json failed its hold-out; positions are compared RELATIVE to the pupil centre.

finding_1_measure.what: The C3b eye profile pools TWO layers. The Phase 2 lid is a real fold, so in the bins 0-4 mm outside the mask margin 715-1,294 of every 1,300-1,700 skin vertices are the lid's INNER face / socket lining, 4.9-7.5 mm inside Tripo. Their median dominates the reading. Outer layer alone: step 0.84 (L) / 0.73 (R) mm. All layers, re-measured: 3.76 / 4.02 (reported 3.83 / 3.94).
finding_1_measure.label: checked

finding_2_real_moat.what: The OUTER surface still sinks. Its inset at 2-3 / 3-4 mm outside the margin is 1.89 / 2.10 (L) and 1.79 / 2.10 (R) mm, against v2's 0.74 / 0.75: 1.15-1.35 mm lower (p90 3.0-3.5 mm). At 4-6 mm it is 0.6-1.0 mm lower, and at 6 mm and beyond it is unchanged. That is a moat round each eye, which is the goggle look.
finding_2_real_moat.label: checked

root_cause.what: feat_eyes' TUNNEL, S1 = max(F, -tunnel) with tunnel = max(M - 1.0, -h - 0.5, h - 6.0), measures the margin distance M along the RADIAL projection from the globe centre. That is right for the lid, which stands on the globe, but wrong for a 6 mm-tall cut. The v2 periocular skin 2-5 mm outside the margin stands 3.0-5.3 mm above the globe, and its radial projection lands INSIDE the margin (median M -0.85 to -0.97 mm). So the tunnel deletes 92-94 % of that skin at 2-3 mm, 76-77 % at 3-4 mm, 41-49 % at 4-5 mm and 14-19 % at 5-6 mm: a cone that widens with height. The 1.9 mm lids refill only its bottom.
root_cause.evidence: cases/cat1/lab/eyes_v3/tunnel_cone.py -> tunnel_cone_v2.json (feat_eyes' own margin_dist / globe_field on skin v2's vertices)
root_cause.label: mechanism checked; 'the cat_p2 moat is this cut' estimated (the emptied bins are exactly the lowered ones; 6 mm and beyond is untouched)

fix: TUNNEL v3 = max(Ma, -h - 0.5, h - (H + 0.5)). Ma is the PLANAR margin distance: p and the margin polygon both projected along the eye axis n onto the plane normal to n (+ outside). The cut is then a prism seen from the front, never a cone, and it stops 0.5 mm above the lid top (Tripo's lid wall top is 1.6-2.3 mm above our globe, so no old skin over the opening stands higher).
Keep the radial M for the LID (its wall rises along the globe normal, REVIEW_eyes B1/B2) and for the socket.
Measure C3b on the outer layer (probe F1).

lid_rim_jagged.root_cause: the lid's 0.45 mm edge round and 1.9 mm wall were evaluated on the 0.5 mm integration grid, about one voxel across the round (PHASE2_ASSESSMENT 1b; the builder's 0.25-0.3 mm preview was smooth)
lid_rim_jagged.fix: resolution contract A20 inside the eye REGION (probe F6); smooth-shaded lid band; rim probe F2. fill_voids must not run on the socket or fornix air: mask it as intended air (NOTES_v3 A20).
lid_rim_jagged.label: root cause cited from the assessment (not re-measured here)

eyelid_wrap_contract.symptom: eyelid_wrap PASSED in the eye builder's run and FAILED in the integrator's run (0 % of sectors, covered 0, visible = every sample)

root_cause.what: The two runs passed different globe_faces. The builder passed feat_eyes.front_faces (front half); the integrator (cat_p2_checks.inventory) passed every face of the closed globe. The probe orients ALL sample normals with one flip, decided by the sign of mean(N . outward). For a whole closed globe that mean is about 0 (-0.002 / +0.001), so sampling noise decides: here it flipped the normals INWARD, every ray ran into the globe's interior, and nothing was hit within 3 mm. Reversing the winding gives the same FAIL, because the flip cancels the winding.
root_cause.evidence: cases/cat1/lab/eyes_v3/wrap_contract.py -> wrap_contract.json: the same cat_p2 mesh and the same probe give (a) whole globe FAIL 0/73,958 covered; (b) front faces PASS, L 23,952 / 38,096 covered, R 24,451 / 38,127, 100 % of sectors; (c) whole globe reversed FAIL
root_cause.label: checked

eyelid_wrap_contract.verdict: The builder's run is right about the mesh: cat_p2's lids do lie on the globe. The integrator's FAIL was a contract error, not a geometry defect.

contract_v3.inputs: {'globe_faces': EVERY face of that side's closed globe, any winding; 'centre_mm': Cs; 'axis': n}. The 'outward' key is dropped.
contract_v3.probe_changes: (1) Orient EACH sample normal radially: N := N * sign(N . (P - Cs)). This is exact because the globe is star-shaped about Cs. (2) Keep the samples with (P - Cs) . n > 0 (the lids lie only on the front half). (3) Keep the result name 'eyelid_wrap', but report it as lid CONTACT (see F4).
contract_v3.proof: probe F3: the three inputs give identical results, and the planted union and fused lid FAIL
contract_v3.owner: engine/checks/inventory_check.py (edit at build time) and the integrator's register call. The spec only states the contract.
